messages:
maya: Heads-up — saw p99 jump in eu-west after we flipped the new kernel-selector + enabled cross-zone fallback yesterday. p95 is stable but p99 is ~2.3x. Not sure if this is batching, KV miss amplification, or the kernel swap.

sre-bot: Deploy notice: kernel-selector v2 -> canary (eu-west) at 2026-03-15T22:10Z. Rolling back on failure enabled.

julian: Can you paste the canary config and the microbatch sizing? also KV hit rates for the canary window?

maya: Canary config snippet: `kernel_selector: v2`, `microbatch_target_tokens: 128`, `fallback: cross-zone`, `batch_timeout_ms: 8`. KV hit rate dropped from 94% -> 71% during the spike window.

kevin: 71% KV hit is a big deal — cross-zone fallback will amplify misses because we serialize KV fetches and warmup across a network hop. That plus a kernel that prefers int8 paths could make tail worse for mixed seq lengths.

li: Confirming kernel detail: v2 prefers int8-cuda-kernel when token_len <= 512 and falls back to fp16 for >512. If routing mixes short and long requests in the same microbatch, the kernel handoff has a scheduling penalty (~5-12ms) that shows up in tails.

olivia: Quick profiling from canary traces (subset):
```
# sample trace lines (shortened)
request_id=rcp-42 seq=64  -> kernel=int8  latency=18ms kv_hit=true
request_id=rcp-43 seq=1024 -> kernel=fp16 latency=42ms kv_hit=false
request_id=rcp-44 seq=48  -> kernel=int8  latency=21ms kv_hit=false
request_id=rcp-45 seq=128 -> kernel=int8  latency=19ms kv_hit=true
# p99 window shows many mixed batches with at least one kv_miss & long seq
```

julian: That matches a hypothesis: mixed sequence lengths + kv misses + kernel-switching -> queuing jitter. Do we have microbatch composition stats (percent of batches that contain >1 kernel type)?

maya: On the canary, ~27% of microbatches were mixed-type. When I forced microbatch to only group by kernel_class (quick test) p99 dropped back closer to baseline (1.1x). But throughput reduced ~9%.

kevin: So it's a SLO vs throughput tradeoff: grouping by kernel_class reduces tail but hurts throughput. For customers with strict p99 we should consider (1) per-tenant routing to local-only, (2) kernel-aware batching that shards microbatch by kernel but keeps overall throughput via smarter multiplexing, or (3) increase microbatching timeout to allow homogenous groups (will increase latency for single requests).

li: Note: kernel-aware batching requires scheduler changes — straightforward but needs careful qdisc tuning to avoid head-of-line blocking. Also KV caching strategy could help: prefix-based partial replication for hot keys across zones to reduce cross-zone miss rate. That’s longer-term.

olivia: Quick numbers: forcing kernel-homogenous microbatches -> p99 delta from baseline: +12% (good), throughput -9%. Reducing microbatch_target_tokens 128 -> 64 -> p99 improves but throughput -15%. Both are knobs with clear cost tradeoffs.

julian: Action items: 1) maya/olivia run a focused A/B in eu-west for two days comparing (kernel-aware batching) vs (microbatch=64). Capture p50/p95/p99, throughput, and cost estimates. 2) kevin/li prototype lightweight kernel-aware scheduler that splits mixed arrivals into parallel microqueues. 3) temporary tactical: route tier-1 customers to local-only fallback until we have mitigation.

maya: Will run the A/B tomorrow and post results. For the immediate window I flipped fallback policy to prefer local-first for the busiest 10% of hosts — monitoring p99 now.

kevin: Thanks — if p99 stabilizes we can roll that as a short-term mitigation. Also adding a note: watch for KV eviction rate when we reduce microbatch size (evictions may increase due to less shared context).

julian: ping me the experiment IDs and I’ll help analyze traces.

olivia: experiment ids: exp-eu-2034-kernel-homogen and exp-eu-2034-micro64. I’ll wire up dashboards.

maya: ok team — will report back with numbers in 48h. :thumbsup:
